Alright, so here we have a wonderful clockwork gentlemen showing advanced robotics before the invention of modern computing. We have another example of this kind of phenomenon on the site in the form of SCP-2776. As such, it may be possible they have the same creator. Recommending the following edits:

Editing the following passage:

Internally, SCP-172 is a staggeringly complex automaton, possessing over two million moving parts, and eighteen million components at last count. Component parts appear to be made of glass, silk, wood, steel, brass, rubber, and several other substances. SCP-172 also has several “modules” that can be installed via a hatch in its chest. These appear to alter behavior, speech, movement, and several parameters based on position in the body cavity and module components. SCP-172 has 46 modules at current count, having built three of these while in Foundation custody. Currently, SCP-172 is loaded with the "engineer" module. Modules have been identified by SCP-172 as "caretaker", "soldier", "medic", "mother", and "king", though this is by no means a comprehensive list (refer to Document #172-2). Under no circumstance are modules to be replaced without O5 level authorization.

To the following:

Internally, SCP-172 is a staggeringly complex automaton, possessing over two million moving parts, and eighteen million components at last count. Component parts appear to be made of glass, silk, wood, steel, brass, rubber, and several other substances. Similarity between this construction and that of SCP-2776 suggest a similar creator or creators. SCP-172 also has several “modules” that can be installed via a hatch in its chest. These appear to alter behavior, speech, movement, and several parameters based on position in the body cavity and module components. SCP-172 has 46 modules at current count, having built three of these while in Foundation custody. Currently, SCP-172 is loaded with the "engineer" module. Modules have been identified by SCP-172 as "caretaker", "soldier", "medic", "mother", and "king", though this is by no means a comprehensive list (refer to Document #172-2). Under no circumstance are modules to be replaced without O5 level authorization.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I'd like to say I really like the basic concept of this article. Its true strength, in my opinion, is not SCP-172 himself, but rather his mysterious origins.

There are plenty of SCPs which appear to function based on magic, super-advanced alien tech, psi abilities, etc. Sometimes, I've got a feeling that half of them can be explained with a blanket "magic is real, and someone used a specific magic spell to create this." Or "it's just future super-tech from space/another dimension." Or "he's a reality bender, like the hundred other reality benders we have."

SCP-172, however, cannot be pigeonholed like this. The implication I'm getting from the article is that SCP-172 is technically not anomalous, and if the Foundation could somehow manage to figure out the impossibly advanced clockwork they would know exactly how he works…

…but, after all, someone had to build him; what's truly anomalous here is the very fact that someone managed to create an advanced AI out of gears and fit them all into a human shell, all this with 19th century technology. How was this accomplished in the first place is really what's inexplicable and intriguing.
